name: confusion
quote: I don't know what's going on.
description: A sense that oneself or another person is in a disordered or uncertain mental state when the situation should be more ordered and certain.
perceptions: Someone (myself or another) should be able to respond appropriately to this situation.
Instead, there's hesitance or perception of inappropriate behavior.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way

guidance.description: Here are some references that may help create more clarity.

variations.name: misinterpretation
variations.description: The sense that someone is talking or acting as if they have an incorrect interpretation of something.
perceptions: That person seems to perceive things in a way that's not aligned to the environment.
results: If there was actually a misinterpretation, the person inside of it cannot see it.
Correcting them may be possible or impossible, obligatory or not worth it.
personOfInterestExperiences: If you realize that you've misinterpreted something, you may feel a sense of failure, embarrassment, laugh it off, or anything inbetween.
examples: A student doesn't understand the homework assignment.
The terse and messy note was not read correctly.
Culture war partisans trying to paint their enemies as negatively as possible.

comparisons.description: With 'misinterpretation', you believe the other person has a 'disordered' (incorrect) mental state for the current situation.

guidance.description: Some references on handling situations where there's a misunderstanding.

variations.name: misremembering
variations.description: The sense that someone is talking or acting as if they have an incorrect memory of something.
perceptions: That person seems to have an incorrect recollection of something.
results: If there was actually a misremembering, the person inside of it cannot see it.
Correcting them may be possible or impossible, obligatory or not worth it.
personOfInterestExperiences: If you realize that you've misremembered something, you may feel a sense of failure, embarrassment, laugh it off, or anything inbetween.
examples: Calling someone by the wrong name.
Getting to the appointment too early because you thought it had been earlier than it was.

comparisons.description: With 'misremembering', you believe the other person has a 'disordered' (incorrect) mental state for the current situation.

guidance.description: Some references on handling situations where you think someone has misremembered something.

variations.name: muddled
variations.description: The sense that someone is talking or acting in a seemingly random and inconsistent way with no clear motivation.
perceptions: That person is acting in a strange and inconsistent way.
results: If the person is actually muddled, they probably cannot see it themselves.
Correcting them may be possible or impossible, obligatory or not worth it.
personOfInterestExperiences: If you realize that you're muddled, you may feel a sense of failure, embarrassment, laugh it off, or anything inbetween.
examples: Someone forgets why they bought too much tape.
Someone with a little too much to drink is talking non-stop nonsense.

comparisons.description: With 'muddled', you believe the other person has a 'disordered' (incorrect) mental state for the current situation.

guidance.description: While a person you perceived as muddled is not always drunk, the same tips may apply.

variations.name: puzzled
variations.description: The sense that you aren't grasping a key pattern that would enable you to make sense of something or solve a problem.
perceptions: I'm faced with a problem or mystery.
I should be able to find the solution.
There's a part of the challenge I'm not understanding.
examples: Not understanding why your pet keeps hiding the toy.
Trying to understand why the modern world makes people crazy.

comparisons.description: With 'puzzled', your own thinking regarding the challenge feels disordered.

variations.name: clinical confusion
variations.description: An abnormal, acute, and persistent lack of effective goal-oriented behavior that may indicate a medical condition.
perceptions: That person is acting in a strange and inconsistent way.
They are going to hurt themselves or someone else.
results: The person may have a medical issue that needs attention.

comparisons.description: Regular confusion is an everyday thing for all of us. Clinical confusion is based on a medical condition that deserves attention.

guidance.description: Many reputable medical websites have guidance on clinical confusion.

commentaries.quote: Confusion is better than idiotic conclusions.
If you are sure you understand everything that is going on, you are hopelessly confused.
Confusion is the first step to knowledge.
The most confused you will ever get is when you try to convince your heart and spirit of something your mind knows is a lie.
Silence is a statement that is open to gross misinterpretation.
The world is a very puzzling place. If you're not willing to be puzzled, you just become a replica of someone else's mind.
